newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slump to lower close on rate woes.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slump to lower close on rate woes.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slumped to a lower close on Tuesday, dragged down by fears of higher interest rates and profit-taking in the popular China plays.
The Hang Seng Index fell 89.62 points, or 0.70 percent, to 12,748.91, shedding most of Monday's 102 point gain. Turnover was HK$7.52 billion compared with HK$9.11 billion on Monday.
"The uncertainty of more U.S. economic statistics coming out ahead of the Fed meeting next week means the buyers are not that tempted yet," said South China Brokerage director Howard Gorges.

"The uncertainty has meant the short-term operators have been inclined to sell and long-term people are waiting to see." The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to meet on March 25 to deliberate interest rates. Gorges said the market had discounted a 25 basis point rise in interest rates.

"I think it has been discounted and people are waiting to buy on the news," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities. He said the Hang Seng Index was likely to find support at 12,600 points.

"Red chips and H-shares have had very significant profit-taking today. Blue chips are a little bit weaker but the selling is not that heavy," added Ho. The H-share index lost 19.50 points, or 1.92 percent, to 997.65.
Conglomerates took a beating on Tuesday. Wharf Holdings Ltd fell HK$1.20 to HK$30.30 and Swire Pacific Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$60.00.
In the property sector, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd ended steady at HK$64.50. It is expected to report strong interim profit growth on Wednesday.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd also ended steady at HK$84.25. It is due to release interim results on Thursday.

Other property shares weakened. Hang Lung Development fell HK$0.55 to HK$14.40. It is scheduled to release its interim results on Thursday. Cheung Kong Holdings closed on a loss of HK$0.50 at HK$70.00.
In the banking sector, shares in HSBC Holdings Plc dropped HK$1.50 to HK$182.50 but Hang Seng Bank Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$82.50.
March Hang Seng Index futures lost 155 points to 12,685.
